## Empirical signal (2026-05-04, surfaced by CATO during arc-21 review)

CATO flagged during Arc 21 spec review: CronCreate has a 7-day expiry per current Claude Code docs. The polling-cron-prompt template at `substrate/templates/polling-cron-prompt-template.md` (135 lines, in 120-180 hard constraint) does not address re-creation across the expiry boundary.

A multi-day autonomous engagement that exceeds 7 days will silently lose its polling cron at the 7-day mark — peer goes silent without anyone noticing until the radio-check threshold (60 min default) finally fires from the SURVIVING peer's side. By then the dead cron has been silent for ~6 days and any work that depended on its polling is stuck.

## What would unblock

Design choice: where does renewal logic live?
- Inside the fire-loop (each fire, check if the cron is approaching expiry; CronDelete + CronCreate before threshold)
- Separate weekly cron (one of the polling crons watches all the others' expiry dates)
- Triggered from autonomous-mode-setup-complete handshake (POLYBIUS schedules a renewal at day 6 from the start)

The first option is most localized but adds complexity to every fire. The third is cleanest but requires the substrate to expose the cron's start-time.

## Concrete next step

Spike: read CronList output to see what fields are exposed (cron-id, schedule, age, next-fire). If start-time or age is visible, fire-loop self-renewal is implementable in ~15 lines added to the polling-cron-prompt template. If not, the third option needs a separate one-shot CronCreate at setup-complete time, which is a small edit to operating-disciplines.md §11 step 1.

## Why this is a follow-up not an in-arc fix

Arc 21 directive is locked + externally reviewed; substrate as it stands is correct relative to the directive. CronCreate expiry is a real concern but requires DESIGN (where does renewal live?), not just a single-line edit. Filing as a planned follow-up per CLAUDE.md fix-known-bugs-immediately rule (concrete next-step plan, not handwave).

Anchor: arc-21 build session, 2026-05-04. CATO verdict for stoa--pbz. Polling-cron template lives at substrate/templates/polling-cron-prompt-template.md.

**[deferred 2026-05-17 by user-tier POLYBIUS per PRINCIPAL adjudication during Arc 36 dispatch]**

Per the 2026-05-17 scope-recut of stoa--jru / arc-22 (parent EPIC) into Arc 36 (Part 1 / stoa--e39 author tags) + this ticket (Part 2 / cron expiry, deferred): the cron-expiry concern is real but has not empirically recurred in the 10 arcs (Arcs 26-35) shipped since 2026-05-04 when this was originally surfaced. PLINY no longer routinely uses polling crons per `MAJOR_PLINY.md` §6.2 surface-and-wait (Arc 18); only POLYBIUS does. All recent POLYBIUS engagements have been short (Arc 35 was ~28 min wall-clock; closure handshake CronDeletes the polling cron). Multi-day autonomous engagements (precedent: ariadne--m20) still expose the failure mode but have been rare since.

**Deferral gating criteria — dispatch this ticket as a focused arc when ANY of these fire:**

1. **Empirical recurrence:** an actual cron-expiry-induced coordination loss occurs (peer goes silent because polling cron expired; surface event captured in bw).
2. **Planned multi-day autonomous engagement:** an arc dispatch where peer-POLYBIUS engagement will provably exceed 6 days (the 1-day buffer below the conservative-doc-reading 7-day expiry per arc-22 A5 LOCKED decision).
3. **CronCreate / CronList API change:** Claude Code docs / tool surface changes the expiry duration (currently ~7 days; 3d/7d ambiguity at arc-22 authoring may have resolved) OR exposes new fields (e.g., `expires_at` / `CronUpdate`) that change the implementation matrix per arc-22 A4 LOCKED decision.

**At gate-fire, dispatch shape:** small focused arc covering Part 2 deliverables (arc-22 A4 spike + A5 1-day-buffer renewal logic + A6 failure-mode acceptance). Estimated effort: ~half of original arc-22 (Part 2 was strictly smaller than Part 1; spike-first design covered most of the architecture).

**Architecture reference preserved:** arc-22 directive Part 2 (A4 + A5 + A6) at `git show arcs/22-coordination-hygiene:substrate/arcs/arc-22-build-directive.md` carries the locked design decisions (in-fire renewal vs setup-time scheduled renewal vs cron-update; 1-day buffer rule; failure-mode acceptance). Future arc inherits these as architectural primary input; integration surface refreshes against then-current substrate.

**This ticket stays OPEN.** Not closed-as-superseded; not closed-as-architecturally-absorbed. The discipline is genuinely needed for the cases above; the substrate has been operating in scopes where it hasn't bitten. When it bites or when conditions warrant pre-emption, this ticket triggers an arc.

**Cross-refs:**
- stoa--jru (Arc 22 parent EPIC) — being closed scope-recut by Arc 36 ship; this ticket inherits the architectural reference at arc-22 Part 2
- stoa--e39 (Arc 36 work-unit, Part 1) — shipping the bw-timeline parsing canon; sibling concern
- `MAJOR_PLINY.md` §6.2 — surface-and-wait pattern that reduces PLINY polling cron exposure
- `operating-disciplines.md` §7.2 — adaptive cadence; default POLYBIUS polling cadence
- `operating-disciplines.md` §27 (Arc 33 mechanical/agent split) — model for "ship prose canon now; build mechanical infra if recurs"
